newsitem.title: UK: UK agriculture urged to explore Eastern Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK agriculture urged to explore Eastern Europe.

text.p: A window of opportunity is open for UK farmers wanting to invest in central and eastern Europe, but it will not be ajar for long, said Jan Cermak, the international business manager of ADAS, the UK's agricultural advice service.
The major problem faced by farms in central and eastern Europe was a lack of working capital and investment, with banks unwilling to offer credit to agriculture.
"Lack of local credit generates scope for foreign investment," Cermak told the Oxford farming conference.
"Good legal back up is essential, but this can be provided by local firms at reasonable rates."

Dutch, Danish and German would-be investors were scouring the countryside, but not the British. And as profitability increased, local farmers were consolidating their operations and developing the capacity to operate without further foreign help, he added.
